match.reason: The bank point only teaches the criminal burden and beyond-reasonable-doubt standard and mentions civil cases only as a contrast, so it does not teach the civil balance-of-probabilities burden and standard that the new point needs.

draft.title: Burden and standard of proof in civil cases
card: The burden of proof is the duty to prove the case. In a civil case, it falls on the plaintiff, who brings the claim.
The standard of proof is how strongly the case must be proved. In a civil case, it is the balance of probabilities.
On the balance of probabilities means it is more likely than not that the plaintiff's version is true. The court asks whether it is more probable than not.
The defendant does not have to prove that they are not liable. If the plaintiff does not meet the standard, the claim fails.
draft.remember: In a civil case, the plaintiff must show their case is more likely true than not.

a.q: Which statement best describes the standard of proof in a civil case?
opts: The plaintiff's version is more likely true than not
The plaintiff's version is certain beyond any doubt
The defendant must show that they are not at fault
The plaintiff's version has some chance of being true
a.why: The balance of probabilities means the plaintiff's case is more probable than not. Certainty beyond any doubt is too high a standard for a civil case, and a mere chance of being true is too low.
a.clue: Think of the words more likely than not.

b.q: Dev sues a builder in the County Court of Victoria for faulty work. The judge thinks it is slightly more likely than not that the work was faulty. What is the result?
opts: Dev meets the standard of proof and can succeed
Dev fails, because the judge has some doubt
Dev fails, because the fault is not proven beyond doubt
Dev must wait for the builder to prove the work was sound
b.why: A civil plaintiff only needs to show the claim is more probable than not. A slight lean in Dev's favour is enough, and some doubt remaining does not defeat the claim. The builder does not have to prove that the work was sound.
b.clue: Does the plaintiff need to remove all doubt?

a.best: The plaintiff's version is more likely true than not

b.best: Dev meets the standard of proof and can succeed
